rationale: One unblinded trial randomized 80 students and reports a favorable menstrual-weakness contrast for fennel soft capsules. An independent extraction reports 38 analyzed controls. Other fatigue results range from inconclusive comparisons to an author abstract for fixed-order fennel-drop treatment. Differences in preparation and population keep the inverse lean at the minimal tier. The independent Delaram fennel-drops trial reports a pooled emotional domain including fatigue. Its overall between-group test and mixed domain do not identify a fatigue effect.

Randomized sulforaphane and glucoraphanin capsule trials conflict on attention: Hei 2022 (n=172 schizophrenia) found inconclusive attention/vigilance change numerically favoring placebo (p=0.263) and Nouchi 2022 (n=144 older adults) found null Coding (p=0.83) and Stroop (p=1) despite Symbol Search p=0.03, while Ghannadi 2025 (n=63 pediatric ADHD methylphenidate adjunct, abstract-only) favored sulforaphane without confirming botanical source; the recorded searches did not locate a raw-broccoli Parkinson attention comparison. The publisher abstract confirms the direction of the parent and teacher inattention ratings and their effect-size notation. Full values, the botanical source and raw exposure remain unverified. The two separate trial registrations report no results.

The immediate crossover favored one chicken–shiitake smoothie spillage component with an inconclusive total and no aspiration observed in either group. Different ingredients and viscosity prevent attribution. The pooled case report and a single public eating-difficulty account supply no roasted shiitake Parkinson swallowing comparison. Three additional original case reports document mechanical esophageal impaction, suspected food-related esophageal symptoms and airway obstruction in multiple sclerosis. These are adverse observations in separate settings with unspecified mushroom preparation. Oven-treated samples show reduced hardness and increased adhesion in laboratory tests, with no comparable oral endpoint. Parkinson manometry used liquid or thickened boluses and provides no tested bridge to the solid ingredient.

Two periodical originals and two ethnobotanical reports clarify food and customary pain uses without measuring response. An oral crude extract lowered writhing in mice, with sedation and movement confounding. Ordinary dietary powder did not effectively reduce swelling in an abstract-level rat study, with no pain estimate. No eligible direction transfers to ground cardamom and Parkinson pain. The publisher preview confirms ground dehusked seeds and leaves conflicting ten-day versus month-long exposure descriptions. The powder arm data and isolated pain outcome remain open.

The spinach-extract trial and its same-cohort thesis planned balance, and the retrieved reports give no balance estimate. Strength outcomes and animal extract studies leave steamed spinach and Parkinson postural instability unresolved. An alternate original thesis edition confirms planned force-platform visits. The clinical article has no supplementary result and disagrees with the registry on dose and placebo. A product description mentioning timed-up-and-go concerns cucumber.
